overview: From 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-21, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 15 new PRs (13 merged), 3 new issues, and 29 active contributors.

topIssues.title: op-node: static peer with /dns4 address cannot reconnect after 7 days once the peer's IP changes
topIssues.author: parkjeongryul
topIssues.body:
**Bug Description**

`op-node` adds `--p2p.static` addresses to the peerstore only once, at startup, with a 7-day TTL (`op-node/p2p/host.go`, `initStaticPeers`). The reconnect loop (`monitorStaticPeers` → `dialStaticPeer`) dials by peer ID only and never re-adds the configured addresses.

After 7 days of uptime the configured `/dns4/...` address expires. The only addresses left are the ones the peer advertised through identify, which inside a Kubernetes pod is the pod IP. If the static peer then restarts and gets a new pod IP, the node keeps dialing the old IP every minute and never reconnects until op-node is restarted.

The peer's Service ClusterIP is advertised only as a side effect of observed-address activation (`ActivationThresh = 4` distinct inbound observers), so you can't count on it. A sequencer that has just restarted and dials its sibling sequencers itself typically has only 3 inbound observers and advertises its pod IP only.

With `--p2p.no-discovery` and several static sequencer peers, each peer drops silently as it is restarted. Nothing is visible until the last one drops. After that the node gets no unsafe payloads and follows L1 derivation only (we observed up to ~93 min of lag).

Nodes using discovery are not affected, because discv5 keeps re-adding addresses from fresh ENRs (24h TTL, refreshed continuously).

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Run op-node A with `--p2p.static=/dns4/<k8s-service>/tcp/9222/p2p/<peer-id>` and `--p2p.no-discovery`, pointing to op-node B behind a Kubernetes Service.
2. Make sure B has fewer than 4 inbound peers, so it advertises only its pod IP.
3. Keep A running for more than 7 days.
4. Restart B's pod so it gets a new pod IP.
5. A logs `error reconnecting to static peer ... dial tcp4 <old-pod-ip>:9222: i/o timeout` every minute and never reconnects.

Results from our cluster:

| A uptime | Addresses in A's peerstore for B | After B restart |
|---|---|---|
| 1 day | DNS + pod IP + ClusterIP | reconnected in 30–55s |
| 17 days | pod IP + ClusterIP | reconnected in 26s (via ClusterIP) |
| 17 days | pod IP only | not reconnected after 19+ min |

**Expected behavior**

A static peer stays dialable through its configured addresses for as long as the process runs. A `/dns4` static address should be re-resolved on every reconnect attempt, regardless of uptime.

**Environment Information:**

- Operating System: Linux (containers on Kubernetes), amd64
- Package Version: op-node v1.19.1 (go-libp2p v0.36.2); the relevant code in `op-node/p2p/host.go` is unchanged on `develop`

**Configurations:**

--p2p.static=/dns4/<chain>-sequencer-node-1.<ns>.svc/tcp/9222/p2p/<id>,/dns4/<chain>-sequencer-node-2.<ns>.svc/tcp/9222/p2p/<id>,/dns4/<chain>-sequencer-node-3.<ns>.svc/tcp/9222/p2p/<id>
--p2p.no-discovery
--p2p.listen.tcp=9222

Topology: RPC replicas dial 3 sequencers one way. The sequencers do not list the replicas as static peers.

**Logs:**

static peer disconnected, reconnecting  peer=16Uiu2HAmVArk...
error reconnecting to static peer  peer=16Uiu2HAmVArk... err="all dials failed * [/ip4/10.131.53.116/tcp/9222] dial tcp4 10.131.53.116:9222: i/o timeout"

This repeats every minute, always with the old pod IP, until the replica op-node is restarted.

**Additional context**

- Suggested fix: re-add `addr.Addrs` to the peerstore in `dialStaticPeer` before `DialPeer`, so the `/dns4` address gets resolved again on each attempt.
- Workaround: restart the dialing node (this resets the 7-day TTL), or call `opp2p_connectPeer` with the full multiaddr.
- Open question: the stale pod IP was still being dialed 19+ min after the disconnect, longer than the 15 min `RecentlyConnectedAddrTTL`. We haven't found out why.

topIssues.title: op-reth: count post-exec rejections on the payload-builder attributes path
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Residual from protocol-team#376 / optimism#23149: the Engine API `newPayload` preflight and block import both count SDM post-exec structural rejections through `reth_op_sdm_post_exec_validation_{failure_,}total`, but the payload-builder attributes path (`forkchoiceUpdated` with transactions, `OpPayloadBuilderAttributes::from_rpc_attrs`) still rejects malformed `0x7D` transactions without incrementing either counter.

Counting there needs the `sdm_metrics` module (`rust/op-reth/crates/evm/src/sdm_metrics.rs`) exposed across crates to `rust/op-reth/crates/payload`, which #23149 deliberately deferred (see its description's "known residual").

Impact: a producer handed malformed post-exec attributes rejects correctly but invisibly — the P1 post-exec alert cannot see this path. Low urgency: the path is producer-local and the rejection itself is safe.

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: keep upstream-clean packages compiling against the latest go-ethereum
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257.

The `opgeth-ratchet` check type-checks against the upstream go-ethereum version op-geth is based on (v1.17.2). Downstream modules that decouple ahead of #20266 move to the *latest* upstream go-ethereum, and Go's minimum version selection then compiles the monorepo's packages against that version too. They need at least v1.17.7 anyway: `op-service/sources` uses the backported `Header.BlockAccessListHash`. But the monorepo code they import has drifted from current upstream APIs, and nothing checks for it.

Against go-ethereum v1.17.7 and v1.17.8 (with the `op-core` transition code from #23525 removed; verified 2026-10-20 on develop@056afb5):

- `op-service/eth`: [`L1ChainConfigByChainID`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-service/eth/config.go#L16-L17) uses `params.HoleskyChainConfig`, which upstream removed. Fix: drop Holesky (shut down).
- `op-core/genesis`: [`storageRoot`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-core/genesis/block.go#L45) calls `StateDB.Commit(block, deleteEmpty, noStorageWiping)`; upstream's is `Commit(rules, block)`. Fix: compute the storage root with `trie.StackTrie` (same API in op-geth and v1.17.8); the existing `directStorageRoot` test helper is the oracle.
- `op-chain-ops/foundry`: the [`StateDB` interface](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-chain-ops/foundry/allocs.go#L35-L40) pins `DumpToCollector`'s return type, which upstream changed to `([]byte, error)`. Fix: take `*state.StateDB` and call `DumpToCollector` as a statement, which compiles against both. Reached by downstream modules through `op-chain-ops/genesis`.

## Gate

Extend `opgeth-ratchet` with a second pass: every package whose import closure contains no allowlisted package must also type-check against a pinned recent upstream go-ethereum release, with no allowlist. The set is derived, not curated, so a package that becomes upstream-clean is covered automatically. Bump the pin with upstream releases. Where a signature change can't be bridged in a shared package, move the code behind a seam (or into the transitional op-geth package) rather than allowlisting it.

Rebasing op-geth onto a newer upstream base isn't an option: the op-geth binary is end of life, and it would pull the drift into the fork-dependent code too.

## Done when

The three sites above compile against both op-geth and the latest upstream go-ethereum, and CI enforces it for every upstream-clean package.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: make op-core/types and op-core/params build against upstream go-ethereum before the cutover
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257.

Downstream Go modules (superchain-registry `ops`, `infra`, `monitorism`, …) can't drop their op-geth `replace` before the final cutover (#20266): anything importing `op-service/eth` (and so `op-service/{rpc,metrics,sources,txmgr,signer,client}`), `op-node/rollup` or `op-chain-ops/genesis` reaches `op-core/types` and `op-core/params`, which use op-geth-only fields. docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md §20 records this as by design. This issue changes that: make those two packages compile against upstream go-ethereum now, and move the op-geth bridging into a transitional package that only the code still driving op-geth imports.

The fork uses are small:

- `op-core/params`: [`GethChainConfig`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-core/params/geth.go#L41-L63) sets `BedrockBlock` … `LagoonTime` and `Optimism` on the go-ethereum config.
- `op-core/types`: [`FromGethReceipt`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-core/types/receipt_consensus.go#L36-L41), [`DeriveFields`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-core/types/receipt_consensus.go#L153-L157) and [`UnmarshalBinary`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-core/types/receipt_consensus.go#L247-L272) read or sync the op-geth receipt's `DepositNonce`/`DepositReceiptVersion` shadow fields.

Removing just those lines makes `op-core/{types,params,genesis,fees,eip1559,predeploys}`, `op-service/{eth,rpc,metrics,sources,txmgr,signer,client}`, `op-node/rollup` and `op-chain-ops/genesis` build against upstream go-ethereum (verified 2026-10-20 on develop@056afb5): against v1.17.2, except `op-service/sources`, which needs the v1.17.7 backport of `Header.BlockAccessListHash`; against v1.17.7+ after the API-drift fixes in #23526.

## Design

- `opparams.ChainConfig.GethChainConfig()` returns only the Ethereum fork schedule — what #20266 already plans for it. The JSON codec is unaffected: its direct OP fields dominate the embedded go-ethereum config ([`chain_config_json.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-core/params/chain_config_json.go#L12-L17)).
- `optypes.Receipt` stops syncing the embedded receipt's shadow fields. `DeriveFields` derives deposit contract addresses from the outer `DepositNonce` itself (its post-cutover form).
- New transitional package, e.g. `op-core/opgeth`, holding only op-geth-only bridging, deleted at the cutover:
  - `ChainConfig(*opparams.ChainConfig) *gethparams.ChainConfig` — `GethChainConfig()` plus the OP fields.
  - `Genesis(*opgenesis.Genesis) *core.Genesis` — the same for genesis.
  - `FromGethReceipt(s)` (moved), plus a reverse helper if a caller hands op-core receipts to op-geth.
- Callers that drive op-geth or read fork fields switch to it; they are already ratchet-allowlisted: the in-process op-geth L2 EL ([sysgo](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-devstack/sysgo/l2_el_opgeth.go#L81), [l2_network](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-devstack/sysgo/l2_network.go#L39), `op-e2e/opgeth`, [e2eutils/setup.go](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-e2e/e2eutils/setup.go#L308), [e2eutils/el/factory.go](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-e2e/e2eutils/el/factory.go#L53)), [`op-service/txplan`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-service/txplan/txplan.go#L341), [`check-karst`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-chain-ops/cmd/check-karst/main.go#L189).
- The `op-core/{types,params}` ratchet entries move to the new package's entries (#20266 reason).
- A deps test (as in [`op-core/superchain/deps_test.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/056afb5f4f1ce2b2482a7d45985ad86173d1c44b/op-core/superchain/deps_test.go)) keeps the new package out of `op-core/*` and `op-service/*`'s downstream-facing packages.
- Update §20 of docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md: downstream modules no longer wait for the cutover on the `op-core/types` edge.

## Risk

The failure mode is silent: under op-geth, a go-ethereum config without the `Optimism` struct has `IsOptimism() == false`, so op-geth treats the chain as L1. The ratchet only checks compilation. Audit every `GethChainConfig()`, `GethGenesis()` and embedded-receipt (`Receipt.Receipt`) reader, and keep `TestToBlockMatchesOpGeth` with the op-geth side built from the new package's `Genesis` until the cutover.

## Done when

- `op-core/types` and `op-core/params` have no ratchet allowlist entries for non-test code.
- `op-service/eth`, `op-node/rollup` and `op-chain-ops/genesis` type-check against upstream go-ethereum at op-geth's base version.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: docs: publish the op-reth reference from gen-cli at v2.4.4 and retire the old CLI tree
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23102 (gen-cli); its diff shows that PR's commits until it merges.

The op-reth CLI reference is 73 pages under Node Operators › Reference, generated at v2.4.1 and three releases behind, with the same Logging and Display blocks reprinted on all 72 command pages and a 60-chain list on most of them, so a search for any common flag returns most of the tree (ethereum-optimism/solutions#1209). This replaces it with the first component on the generated, versioned reference the content guide specifies: 15 pages under `reference/op-reth/v2.4`, generated by gen-cli from the published `op-reth:v2.4.4` image in 13 seconds, with an index, one page per top-level command whose nested subcommands are headings, and a global-options page for the three sections every command repeated. The Reference tab now exists with the op-reth dropdown and its v2.4 version entry.

Effect on users: every old URL redirects. Nested subcommands land on the anchor of their heading (`db/checksum/mdbx` → `db#checksum-mdbx`), verified live with `mint dev` along with the root and overview redirects. The 69 older redirects that already pointed into the deleted tree are re-targeted so no redirect chains. The hand-written orientation page moves to Node Operators › Guides › Configuration ("Understanding the op-reth CLI"), since nothing under `reference/` is hand-written, and nine pages that linked into the old tree now link to the new one. The `op-reth node` page is 1,700 lines instead of the old tree's combined 17,700, and the chain list appears once, as a pointer to the superchain-registry. op-reth's flag catalog moves from three releases behind to current.

Effect on maintainers: `gen-op-reth-cli` is deleted; gen-cli regenerates this line with `--component op-reth --tag <tag> --image auto`, and `--check` verifies it. The nav, redirect, reference and link-policy lints pass on this branch with its own lint scripts (#23102 now carries the nav-lint change that understands `dropdowns`/`versions`, identical to #23091's, so this no longer waits on #23091). Until the tag-triggered regeneration job lands (ethereum-optimism/solutions#1518, Phase 2.2), a new op-reth release is regenerated by hand; the old tree had no working automation either (the README described one that was never registered), so this gap is not new.

Review: the deletion-reviewer agent swept the whole repository for references to the deleted URLs, nav group and generator, and verified one redirect per deleted URL, every anchored destination against the target page's headings, no chains, and no other generator or asset referencing the old tree. It found one dead link in `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md` step 9 of the reth-bump procedure (fixed), three descriptions that still said the reference was imported from the source tree or that subcommands get their own pages (fixed), and the nav-lint dependency above (resolved by carrying the change in #23102). No findings dismissed.

Redirect destinations name the `v2.4` line. When a new minor line ships and becomes the default, those redirects still resolve but land on v2.4; retargeting them is a one-line job for the regeneration workflow and is tracked with the versioning work rather than done here.

Refs ethereum-optimism/solutions#1518 (Phase 2, first migration); closes the collapse asked for in ethereum-optimism/solutions#1209. Depends on #23102 and #23091.

topPRs.title: op-reth!: demonstrate optimistic parallel execution PoC
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
This PoC explores reducing op-reth execution latency by speculating on independent transactions while preserving canonical transaction order, state, receipts, fees, and SDM settlement. It covers Engine validation, historical execution, forced transactions, pool sequencing, and subblock continuation. **Sequential execution remains the default; parallel and rolling execution are opt-in.**

The [PoC write-up](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/POC.md) covers the high-level architecture, low-level decisions, results, and production gates. The [README](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/README.md) documents configuration and reproduction commands.

The central choice is bounded speculation against immutable snapshots of **committed state only**. One coordinator validates dependencies and commits in order; stale or failed attempts execute once canonically. This avoids speculative worker-to-worker dependencies and cascading rollback. Independent worker-local readers remove coordinator read messages, and optional rolling scheduling overlaps ordered commit with further execution. Broker windows remain the compatibility fallback.

Protocol fee credits are settled in order without manufacturing dependencies between otherwise independent transactions. SDM observation is transaction-local; refund evaluation and policy updates remain ordered and commit-only. The authoritative selector controls inclusion, with `on_commit` before its next `next()`. Resource limits cover outstanding attempts, speculative gas, dependencies, outputs, and retained snapshot versions. Shared worker permits, generation checks, and reader-teardown barriers govern cancellation and competing operations.

| Synthetic comparison | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Final rolling vs sequential: independent compute | 3.1x at 4 workers; 4.4x at 8 |
| Final rolling vs sequential: stock BN254 pairings | 3.7x at 4 workers; 6.3x at 8 |
| Independent readers vs broker windows: storage | 5-6x at 4 workers |
| Rolling vs direct windows | 14-35% lower storage latency; 13% lower expensive-policy latency at 4 workers |

These are separate local in-memory experiments using an optimized test profile; their ratios are not cumulative. Cheap storage often remains faster sequentially. Contention, read amplification, retained snapshots, serial policy work, and tail latency limit the gains. No production database or end-to-end replay speedup is claimed. See the [performance report and raw data](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/optimistic-parallel-execution/rust/op-reth/crates/parallel/benchmarks/session-summary.md).

This draft depends on [ethereum-optimism/reth#10](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/pull/10). Before production: land reviewed source hooks; independently review and fuzz consensus-sensitive paths; replay representative chain ranges against known roots; measure release-build latency, memory, database I/O, and competing builds; integrate the real SDM policy; and complete shadow soak and canary rollout. Upstream borrowed/Arc configuration wrappers currently retain broker reads, and opaque Engine precompile-cache wrappers require canonical precompile fallback. Both remain documented compatibility limitations.

BREAKING CHANGE: Downstream Rust integrations constructing `OpBlockExecutionCtx` must supply `parallel_candidates` (empty for sequential execution) or use `..Default::default()`. Runtime-bearing executor factories and `OpExecutorBuilder` require explicit cloning instead of `Copy`; custom `OpTxEnv` implementations need `Clone`; generic `OpBlockExecutor` users must carry its `Evm` bound. Construct `OpHandler` with `OpHandler::new()` instead of external struct literals. No Engine API wire or database migration is introduced.

Validation: 603 affected execution/integration/txpool/CLI tests pass (3 skipped), including the rebased txpool affordability changes. The saved 121-configuration rolling benchmark checks output parity. Formatting, scoped Clippy with warnings denied, rustdoc, affected `no_std` builds, and the upstream-mirror check pass.

Rust correctness, deletion/write-preservation, and reth dependency/mirror reviews completed. Provider-failure propagation has regression coverage through actual EVM errors and cancellation races. The reth wrapper limitation above remains an open production follow-up. Full workspace `just lint` is blocked in the unchanged `gmp-mpfr-sys` dependency by missing `m4`; scoped checks are reported separately above.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: prove below-head interop references with log-commitment batches
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
PR 2 lets the SP1 consolidation check a message to a block below the initiating chain's local safe head against a log-commitment entry instead of that block's receipts. This PR makes the proposer (and the executor test tool) use it, so referencing many large blocks no longer makes one timestamp unprovable.

The proposer scans a game's messages at proof time and picks one path per game: receipts when every request's bound fits, otherwise the table path, where it proves each referenced block once in batches before any consolidation and attaches the covering batch proofs to each request. Requests over the PGU budget, the witness cap, or 4 GiB of stdin are refused, and on the table path the proposer applies these checks to the scan-fixed part of each request before any batch request. `LOG_PATH=receipts` turns the table path off.

The proposer now needs `<vkey>.log.bin.gz` next to the other two artifacts, so prestates published before the log program (`v0.0.1`, `v0.0.2-rc.1`) cannot be loaded. New settings: `LOG_PATH`, `LOG_PROOF_STRATEGY`, `LOG_CYCLE_LIMIT`, `LOG_GAS_LIMIT` (10¹¹).

Testing: unit tests for the scan, path choice, batching, retries, and request checks; ELF-gated tests that pin each estimator at or above measured PGU; interop acceptance with a below-head reference (Kona, SP1 native core, full ELF); a ZK acceptance test on the table path with the mock provider. The pre-check is unit-tested, but no test fails on the baseline at its call site. Gaps: a replaced head's cost is not calibrated (no state in the fixture), executor memory at the caps is not yet measured on Linux, the canary still takes the receipts path (proofs-team#30), and there is no persistent batch cache (proofs-team#31).

topPRs.title: op-reth,kona-node!: build derived payloads in a payload service wrapper
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Alternative to #23447: same fix, built in a payload service wrapper instead of `OpEngineApi`, with no reth changes.

op-reth only found out that a derived block's transactions were invalid in its asynchronous payload build, after `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` had already answered VALID. An invalid forced transaction was skipped, so op-reth built a block that the fault proof rejects. An invalid `0x7D` failed the build instead, so `engine_getPayload` returned an error, the rollup node retried the same attributes forever and the safe head stalled.

`DerivedPayloadServiceBuilder` wraps a payload service builder. For `noTxPool` attributes that carry a non-deposit transaction, the service it spawns builds the payload exactly once, with op-reth's payload builder and the engine tree's resources, before it answers the engine's `BuildNewPayload` command. The engine awaits that answer in `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` and turns a failure into `-38003`, so op-node and kona-node (fixed here) replace the block with a deposits-only one. Every other command goes to the wrapped service. `OpNode` wraps its payload service; op-reth-premium opts in with a one-line wrap.

- The build runs on a blocking task. The engine tree doesn't wait for it; only the forkchoiceUpdated response does.
- `engine_getPayload` resolves the built payload like a payload job's and emits `Events::BuiltPayload` on the first resolution, as reth's service does, so `engine_newPayload` doesn't execute the block a second time.
- A build that fails for a node-local reason (missing state, provider error, panic) is never `-38003`; it goes to the wrapped service with the engine's leases. If that fails too, `engine_getPayload` fails and the rollup node retries.
- A retried request joins the running build or gets the built payload.
- For derived attributes with an invalid transaction, `debug_executePayload` returns the witness up to that transaction, where the fault proof program stops, instead of the witness of a block without it.

Supersedes #23188, whose kona-node fix and acceptance test this carries. Compared with it, with an earlier private fix (optimism-private@ed9e4d8) and with #23447:

| | #23188 | ed9e4d8 | #23447 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Where it checks | payload job generator, at job creation | `OpEngineValidator::validate_payload_attributes_against_header` | `OpEngineApi`, in `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` | payload service wrapper, at `BuildNewPayload` |
| Derived attributes covered | `0x7D` only | all with a non-deposit tx | all with a non-deposit tx (one-line switch to all `noTxPool`) | all with a non-deposit tx (one-line switch to all `noTxPool`) |
| Executions per derived block | 1 | 2 (validate, then build) | 1 | 1 |
| op-reth-premium | not covered (own job generator) | covered | covered | covered with a one-line wrap |
| Invalid forced tx skipped (fault-proof mismatch) | yes | fixed | fixed | fixed |
| kona-node fix + acceptance test | yes | no | yes | yes |
| Upstream changes | none | none | reth hook (ethereum-optimism/reth#16) | none |
| Costs | blocks the payload service while building; copy of reth's payload service builder | double execution; breaking `Evm` parameter on `OpEngineValidator` | copies reth's attribute checks; FCU serialized by a lock | payload services must opt in |

Downsides of this approach:
- A payload service that isn't wrapped isn't covered: premium and third-party node builders must opt in.
- It proxies reth's `PayloadServiceCommand` enum; a new command upstream needs a match arm here (a compile error, not a silent gap).
- `Events::BuiltPayload` must fire exactly when reth's service fires it, or `engine_newPayload` re-executes the block.
- `-38003` carries no reason; it is only in op-reth's logs.
- After a node-local failure, the wrapped service's fallback build runs without the tree's execution cache and state root task (it keeps the leases).

Review agents (Rust, security) ran; their findings are fixed except, to confirm:
- The switch to all `noTxPool` attributes stays a `const`, as that choice is still open.
- A payload id collision with different attributes is only partly handled: a request joins a build or a built payload only if the attributes match too, but `engine_getPayload` looks payloads up by id. Ids hash every attribute field, and reth trusts them the same way.
- `Events::Attributes` is emitted when a derived build starts, as reth does when it creates a job, so after a node-local failure the wrapped service emits it again. Nothing in reth consumes it.
- After the shutdown signal, a forkchoiceUpdated with attributes gets `-38003`, as with reth's own payload service.
- Not changed here, as in #23447: a transient error while kona-node builds the deposits-only replacement is critical, and kona-node gates the replacement on the L2 timestamp, op-node on the L1 origin's.

The kona-node and acceptance-test commits are the ones from #23447, where the Go and derivation-batch reviewers ran.

BREAKING CHANGE: op-reth answers `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` with `-38003` when the transactions of derived attributes make the block invalid. op-node handles this. kona-node needs the change in this PR, otherwise it retries and stalls the safe head, so upgrade both together. `OpNodeComponentBuilder`'s default payload service builder is now `DerivedPayloadServiceBuilder<OpPayloadServiceBuilder>`; nodes that replace the payload service must wrap theirs in `DerivedPayloadServiceBuilder` to be covered.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: docs: add gen-cli, one generator for the versioned component CLI reference
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
The docs have three generators for component flags with three page shapes (gen-flags from Go source for five services, gen-op-reth-cli from op-reth's `--help`, gen-deploy-config for the deploy schema) and none at all for kona-node, op-supernode or op-deployer. The content guide's "Component reference" section (#23091) specifies one shape for every component, versioned by release line under a Reference tab. This is the generator that produces it; without it the convention is a document with nothing enforcing it.

`scripts/gen-cli/` walks a release artifact's `--help` tree (`--image` runs the published Docker image, `--bin` a local binary such as op-deployer's release tarball, `--help-json` a recording for tests), parses clap and op-service's urfave/cli help template into one model, and emits one release line of one component: an index page, one page per top-level command with nested subcommands as headings (so `db#checksum-mdbx` still deep-links), and a global-options page for the option sections at least half the commands print identically, which the per-command verbatim help then omits. It splices the Reference tab, the component dropdown and the Mintlify version entry into `docs.json`, records a manifest keyed by tag (or commit for the `develop` line) with a tree hash, and `--check` fails on any drift or hand edit. On the committed op-reth help tree, 72 commands become 15 pages.

Effect on users: none yet. No pages are generated here; the per-component migrations follow, starting with op-reth at v2.4.4 from its published image, each with redirects built from the generator's `--page-map`. Effect on maintainers: one tool and one page shape to learn instead of three; gen-flags and gen-op-reth-cli stay until their components have migrated.

Verified: 61 tests replaying pruned recordings of the op-reth and op-node help trees (both parsers, hoisting, page tree and anchors, escaping, determinism, nav ordering, write-then-`--check` round trip); rendered with `mint dev` against a full op-reth v2.4 and op-node develop generation (tables, anchors, Accordion, develop banner, version switcher); the nav, redirect and reference lints from #23091 pass against that generated tree. Two things this surfaced: Mintlify serves a folder's `index.mdx` at `/folder/index`, matching this site's existing convention, so the root page URL carries `index`; and reth's help text already backslash-escapes `<IP>`, which a naive table escaper doubles into a JSX tag.

Rejected alternative: parsing flag definitions from source per framework (what gen-flags does). It renders richer tables for Go but needs a toolchain per language and drifts from what the released binary accepts; `--help` from the artifact is the one surface every component exposes identically and is what the convention names as the source of truth.

Review: a code-review agent exercised the generator against the fixtures, a freshly built develop op-node, and probe inputs, and reported eight groups of findings; all are fixed here and none dismissed. The two that mattered most: clap's `--flag[=<VALUE>]` shape (op-reth's `--logs-otlp`, `--tracing-otlp`) was not recognised, so those flags vanished and their text leaked into the previous flag's row; and the hoist-strip on verbatim help matched clap headers only, so it would have been a no-op for any Go service. Also fixed: `--verbosity...` absorbing its ellipsis, aliases dropped from both frameworks, parenthesised urfave defaults truncated, a bare `OPTIONS` header lower-cased, silent skips of unparseable Commands lines (now errors), backticks inside code spans, the anchor slug algorithm (now github-slugger's), reserved page names, `--check` missing nav default/tag drift, the op-node chain list surviving line wrapping, percent-encoded paths, locale-dependent sorting, and `pnpm test:gen-cli` crashing under tsx. Pre-existing and left as is: a nested command whose name equals a section title would get a de-duplicated heading slug the page map does not predict; no component has one.

Refs ethereum-optimism/solutions#1518 (Phase 2). Depends on #23091 for the lint that guards the generated tree; independent of #23100.
